claims: For 128-bit PEXEW, output words low-to-high are source [2,1,0,3].
For 128-bit PEXCW, output words low-to-high are source [0,2,1,3].
For 128-bit PROT3W, output words low-to-high are source [1,2,0,3].
The candidate _MM_SHUFFLE selectors encode the mappings using selector argument order (z,y,x,w) with destination lanes selecting (w,x,y,z).
The mmi-shuffle-03 probe covers rd==rt, rt==0, rd==0, four basis vectors and 10,000 deterministic random inputs, for three helpers plus PS2_PROT3W macro; candidate mismatches are zero in all groups.
The probe proves full emulator or game behavior.

evidence.text: Sony EE manual explicitly assigns PEXEW source lanes [2,1,0,3], PEXCW [0,2,1,3], PROT3W [1,2,0,3] to destination lanes low-to-high, at pages 201,199,260. https://docs.alexrp.com/mips/ee_insns.pdf

Intel SDM PSHUFD: each two-bit immediate field selects the source doubleword for a destination lane; 128-bit form operates on four low-lane doublewords. https://www.intel.com/content/dam/develop/external/us/en/documents/319433-024-697869.pdf

Pinned PCSX2 MMI.cpp source independently assigns PEXEW [2,1,0,3], PEXCW [0,2,1,3], PROT3W [1,2,0,3], and uses early return on Rd=0. https://github.com/PCSX2/pcsx2/blob/81526d4dc7cc70e4ae75abb35a789417456c6d43/pcsx2/MMI.cpp

mmi-shuffle-03/result.json: four test groups x 40016 checks each; baseline mismatches [20008,20008,20004,20004], candidate mismatches [0,0,0,0]. Inputs include basis patterns and 10,000 MT19937 values, crossed with modes rd==rt, separate rd/rt, rt==0, rd==0. Tests three generated helpers and PS2_PROT3W macro wrapper, using SSE2NEON, UBSan. Receipt explicitly says synthetic lane mapping only, no game routine executed, no complete translator/game equivalence.

Candidate selectors: PEXEW _MM_SHUFFLE(3,0,1,2); PEXCW _MM_SHUFFLE(3,1,2,0); PROT3W _MM_SHUFFLE(3,0,2,1). In the Intel intrinsic convention _MM_SHUFFLE(z,y,x,w) forms immediate fields such that output lanes 0..3 select input lanes w,x,y,z.
